content.text: {"label":"system_slowness","explanation":"Payments handle time jumped from about forecast (277-326 s) to 352 s at 11:00 and 479 s at 11:15, roughly +53% over forecast. Service level fell to 54% and then 40%, and abandons rose from 7 to 25. Volume is close to forecast (+0.7% for the day; 11:00 was -8%, 11:15 was +8%). The reason mix barely moved: no reason exceeds 1.2x normal, so no single call type is driving it. Attendance is normal (2 sick vs about 2.8 usual) and agents on phones are near plan, so it is not a staffing shortfall. A sudden, broad rise in handle time with no volume or absence driver points to slow payments systems. No incident has been logged yet, so this should be confirmed with IT. General is running mildly above forecast (+8%) and its service level is uneven (70-87%), but it is not alarming.","plan_name":"Payments capacity recovery during slow handling","rationale":"At about 1.5x handle time, payments effectively needs about 50% more agent capacity, so the plan stacks capacity levers. It delays payments breaks now to cover the immediate dip, which is free. It cancels payments coaching for the afternoon. It runs two consecutive overtime offers from 12:00 (the earliest arrival) to 16:00; at about 40% acceptance that is roughly 8 agents per block and about Rs 5,800 in total, well within the Rs 15,000 budget. It moves only 2 cross-skilled agents from general, because general's service level is borderline. It deflects status-type payment calls to chat (about Rs 2,500) and offers callbacks to callers facing long waits. The outage message is not used because no outage is confirmed.
